reviews.review_description: I picked this up because it looked different, and now I've somehow ended up speed running it. After learning the routes and how to stay one step ahead of the Overseer's light I felt confident I could run this game.   My current best is 3:46:52, and it's amazing how much time you save making smarter decisions instead of just moving faster. This game has a surprising amount of depth, and every mistake teaches you something for your next attempt.  If you enjoy a game that rewards practice and real time planning, this game is incredibly satisfying.

developer_response.body: Holy crap!  You were able to speed run the game already and that's beating our time.. Do you sleep?  Honestly we put speedrunning in High Ground but was unsure if anyone would do it.  This is fantastic and you made my month.  Please submit that run to speedrun.com, I think you would be the first!  Thank you.

reviews.review_description: Honestly, I didn't expect a game without any shooting or traditional combat to get my heart rate up this much! Panic sets in when the energy level alert starts sounding and you have to scramble to find the nearest portal. Not to mention the ominous warning of the overseer's light!  It took me a few tries to get the hang of it, but the challenge, and the feeling of being so close keeps you engaged.

developer_response.body: Every failed run teaches you something 😄. I'm really glad it clicked after a few tries and thank you for sticking with it and for leaving this review — it means everything to us. See you at the summit! 🏔️

reviews.review_description:
High Ground is a brilliantly unique stealth experience where you’re the intruder, clawing your way to the summit of a towering mountain—all while avoiding detection by the Overseer, a relentless, Sauron-like eye that never blinks! Your energy drains fast, so you’ll need to strategically warp between portals to recharge, making every move a tense puzzle of timing and precision.
The atmosphere is incredibly immersive, with the Overseer’s gaze feeling like a physical weight on your back. The single-player mode is already a standout, but the addition of a multiplayer mode? Chef’s kiss! It’s a stroke of genius that boosts replayability to stratospheric levels.
If you love stealth games with a fresh twist and heart-pounding tension, High Ground is an absolute must-play. A masterclass in tension and execution! 🎮✨

developer_response.body:
Wow! Masterclass in tension and execution' is going on our wall. Genuinely. Thank you for taking the time to write this so thoughtfully — reviews like this are what keep small studios going.

See you at the summit! 🏔️

reviews.review_description:
This was a chance purchase. I was bored, looking for something new to play, and High Ground looked interesting enough.
First off, I think it's a little miscategorized. Personally, I wouldn't call it a shooter. Yes, you kind of have a weapon, but that's not really what the game is about.
It's honestly hard to describe. Your goal is to find a path to the top of each level and disable the Overseer, but getting there is the challenge. You have to carefully choose where to move, manage your energy, avoid enemies, and think several steps ahead. It's a mix of strategy, puzzle-solving, and action that somehow just works.
The more I played, the more it clicked. I get it now. Every level feels like you're solving a puzzle while under pressure, and it's incredibly satisfying when you finally figure out the right route to the top.
That being said, this isn't an easy game. I've found myself yelling, "WTF?!" more than once, then immediately jumping right back in because I had to figure it out.
The screenshots and trailer don't really explain what the game is. But after playing it, they suddenly make sense.
If you're looking for a traditional VR shooter, this probably isn't it. But if you enjoy strategy games, I definitely recommend giving High Ground a try.

developer_response.body:
This review means more to us than you probably realize.
You put your finger on something we've wrestled with since day one — High Ground is genuinely hard to categorize and even harder to explain before you've played it.
Reviews like this help future players know what they're actually getting into.

reviews.review_description: A friend told me to get this. I'm not really in to the whole sci-fi thing and I hate shooters.  Turns out... this isn't really a shooter at all.  After a small learning curve, I've fallen in love with this game.  Its not a deep game but its very challenging and more fun than it should be.  Total sleeper hit of the year.  BTW - the developers owe me a new pair shorts.  I was paniking looking for a hiding spot, I turned around and a wraith was there screaming at me.  I need a new pair of shorts.

developer_response.body:
Ha! We owe you a pair of shorts AND an apology — but honestly, that Wraith doing its job perfectly.  😂

We love that you came in skeptical and stayed for the panic. 
Thank you for giving it a chance and thank you for the review. It means the world to us.

reviews.review_description:
So - there’s basically a lighthouse the middle of the map.  And as it rotates, it also moves up and down.  If it finds you, you start losing energy, it makes a terrible noise, and it stays trained on you until you can get into cover.  It’s the closest you can feel to having the Eye of Sauron on you without being in Middle Earth.  

So - your goal, of course, is to get to the top of the lighthouse.  You do this by running, avoiding the eye - and teleporting to platforms that will restore your energy.   Also avoiding enemies.  Enemies are bad - but less terrifying than the eye.  When you inevitably fail, you start back at the bottom again.

So basically, you have to learn the best routes, while avoiding the eye, and dodging any enemies, and teleporting between platforms, and not being off a platform for too long because you slowly lose energy the longer you’re not on a platform. 

It’s totally unique and I’ve never quite played anything like it - but I think it’s a a lot of fun.  And if this sounds like something you might enjoy, you owe it to yourself to check it out!

developer_response.body: Wow!  What a great review and thank you for taking the time to write this out so thoughtfully.

reviews.review_description: If you like thrills and working under pressure, this is the game for you! I’m terrible at these types of games to be honest, but once I finally made it to the second pad, I felt a sense of accomplishment and am eager to keep getting better. It’s fun hiding from the overseer and planning your next dash. I’m excited to share with my friends so we can play together. Great game!

developer_response.body:
The fact that you describe yourself as terrible at these games and still got hooked means so much to us. High Ground was always meant to reward persistence  — and you just proved it works.

Can't wait for you to bring your friends in — the multiplayer chaos when everyone is scrambling for the same platforms while the Overseer hunts all of you simultaneously is something else entirely. 😄

Thank you for giving it a chance and for sharing your experience. See you at the summit! 🏔️

reviews.review_title: All to Think About,  Before  Sunrise
reviews.review_description:
I’m seriously impressed with High Ground on Meta Quest. It’s a real-time strategy game in the truest sense—where decisions happen in seconds, not minutes or hours.

Do you run or wait? Every movement costs energy, which you can recharge on platforms scattered throughout the environment. But there’s another layer: you can create a portal to those platforms from a distance, giving you a way to escape or reposition. On the platform, you can choose to charge up faster, but doing so comes at a cost—it increases the time before your next portal becomes available and can make you wait longer before creating another one.

So every move becomes a calculation.

Then the enemies come after you. Do you keep running, or use your EMP to disable them? You only get one EMP at a time, and fully charging on a platform restores it—but do you really have the luxury of standing still that long when something is chasing you?

That’s what makes High Ground so much fun. Nothing happens in turns. Nothing waits for you. You’re constantly making decisions, balancing energy, portals, EMPs, movement, and risk—all in real time.

And there’s one more problem: sunrise.

I took too long on my first attempt and failed because I hadn’t reached the top before the sun came up. That was the moment I realized just how much this game is asking you to manage simultaneously.

High Ground takes a lot to think about—and gives you very little time to think about it. And somehow, that’s exactly what makes it so compelling.
